candidates.title: [Bug]: closed record with an optional `never` field is not a subtype of the same record without it
[Bug]: list returned by `map:keys()` has no filler value (storing past the end panics "no filler value")
candidates.body:
### Description
`map:keys` returns "a new list of all keys" with return type `string[]`; the runtime even gives it inherent type `string[]`. Storing past its end should fill the gap with `""` (the filler for `string`), as it does for a list constructor, but it panics with `no filler value`.

**Spec:** §7.15.1: "When a store is performed on an lvalue referring to a member k of a list value and the length of the list is n and k is > n, then each member with index i for each ≤ i < k is filled in, by using the FillMember abstract operation". §5.9.1 FillMember succeeds when the inherent type allows member k and a filler exists for the member type; `string` has filler `""`.

Control: `string[] s = ["a"]; s[3] = "z";` correctly prints `["a","","","z"]`.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    map<int> m = {a: 1};
    string[] ks = m.keys();
    ks[3] = "z";
    io:println(ks); // @output ["a","","","z"]
}
```
Actual: `error: no filler value at main(...:6)`.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ fb67e6e53730b6d658883c35937e01b8a183ca9a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, built with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Langlib (`lang.map`)

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related but different: #1147, #1050 (other filler issues).

candidates.title: [Bug]: `array:fromBase64` / `array:fromBase16` reject whitespace allowed by Base64/Base16 literals
candidates.body:
### Description
The langlib docs say `fromBase64`'s `str` "must consist of the characters `A..Z`, `a..z`, `0..9`, `+`, `/`, `=` and whitespace as allowed by a Ballerina Base64Literal", and `fromBase16`'s "the characters `0..9`, `A..F`, `a..f` and whitespace as allowed by a Ballerina Base16Literal".

The spec grammar allows `WS` (`WhiteSpaceChar := 0x9 | 0xA | 0xD | 0x20`) between every digit: `HexGroup := WS HexDigit WS HexDigit`, `Base64Group := WS Base64Char WS Base64Char WS Base64Char WS Base64Char`.

nutcracker returns an error for spaces/tabs in both functions, and for any whitespace (even `\n`) in `fromBase16`. Only `\n`/`\r` happen to work for `fromBase64`, which is inconsistent.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;
import ballerina/lang.array;

public function main() {
    io:println(array:fromBase64("3q2+ 7w==")); // @output [222,173,190,239]
    io:println(array:fromBase64("3q2+\n7w==")); // @output [222,173,190,239]
    io:println(array:fromBase16("de ad\tbe\nef")); // @output [222,173,190,239]
    io:println(array:fromBase16("dead\nbeef")); // @output [222,173,190,239]
}
```
Actual:
```
error("failed to decode base64 string")
[222,173,190,239]
error("failed to decode base16 string")
error("failed to decode base16 string")
```

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ fb67e6e53730b6d658883c35937e01b8a183ca9a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, built with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Langlib (`lang.array`)

### Related issue(s) (optional)
None found.

candidates.title: [Bug]: type cast does not pass its contextually expected type to an inferred `<>` typedesc call
candidates.body:
### Description
A call to a dependently-typed function (`cloneWithType`, `fromJsonWithType`) used as the operand of a type cast fails with "cannot infer typedesc argument for parameter 't': no contextually expected type". The same call without the cast compiles and works.

**Spec:** §6.20 type cast expression: "The contextually expected type for expression is the intersection of the contextually expected type of the type-cast-expr and the type described by the type-descriptor." For `float|error h = <float|error> v.cloneWithType();` the operand's expected type is `float|error`, so `t` should be inferred as `float` (unifying `t|error` with `float|error`). Even `<float> v.cloneWithType()` with no outer context has expected type `float`.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    anydata v = 7;
    float|error h = <float|error> v.cloneWithType();
    io:println(h); // @output 7.0
}
```
Actual:
```
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: cannot infer typedesc argument for parameter 't': no contextually expected type
```
Control: `float|error h = v.cloneWithType();` prints `7.0`. `float h = <float> check v.cloneWithType();` and `j.fromJsonWithType()` in the same position fail the same way.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ fb67e6e53730b6d658883c35937e01b8a183ca9a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, built with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Type checker (dependently-typed functions / type cast)

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related (same symptom under `trap`): #1385

candidates.title: [Bug]: function with more than one `<>` inferred typedesc parameter is accepted
candidates.body:
### Description
The spec restricts the `<>` default to at most one parameter per function, but nutcracker accepts a declaration with two such parameters (and calls to it type-check).

**Spec:** defaultable-param: "It is also possible for the default to be specified as <>; ... It is allowed only when the parameter name to which the default value applies is referenced in the return-type-descriptor, as described below, and is allowed for at most one parameter in a function."

The other `<>` restrictions (non-typedesc parameter, parameter not referenced in return type) are already diagnosed correctly.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
function g(typedesc<anydata> t = <>, typedesc<anydata> u = <>) returns t|u|error = external; // @error

public function main() {
}
```
Actual: compiles with no diagnostic. A caller `int|error x = g();` also type-checks.
Expected: a compile-time error on the declaration.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ fb67e6e53730b6d658883c35937e01b8a183ca9a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, built with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Type checker (function definitions)

### Related issue(s) (optional)
None found.
